You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

import os,glob,re,json
d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n')
G={}
for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
    k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
    rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
    if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
        G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
print(sorted(G))
I=G['Demo pair 1 input']; O=G['Demo pair 1 output']
from collections import Counter
print(Counter(v for r in I for v in r), Counter(v for r in O for v in r))
print([(i,j,I[i][j]) for i in range(len(I)) for j in range(len(I[0])) if I[i][j]!=8])
print([(i,j,O[i][j]) for i in range(len(O)) for j in range(len(O[0])) if O[i][j]!=8])

import collections,json,re
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load()

def f(I):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0]); out=[r[:] for r in I]
    g=collections.defaultdict(list)
    for i in range(H):
        for j in range(W): g[I[i][j]].append((i,j))
    # objects: non-bg colors
    objs=[]
    for col,vv in sorted(g.items()):
        if I[vv[0][0]][vv[0][1]]==8: continue
        objs.append((col,vv))
    rects=[o for o in objs if len(o[1])>=50]   # rectangular block
    lines=[o for o in objs if len(o[1])<50]    # diagonal line(s)
    assert len(lines)==1
    col,vv=lines[0]; pts=sorted(vv,key=lambda p:p[0])
    dr,dc=pts[1][0]-pts[0][0], pts[1][1]-pts[0][1]
    assert dr==dc and dr!=0
    R1,R2=pts[0],pts[-1]
    # which side of the line is the rect? test both endpoints for sign of (p-R)*n
    def side(p):
        v=(p[0]-R1[0])*dr-(p[1]-R1[1])*dc
        return v>0
    s=side(tuple(rects[0][1][0]))
    # endpoints nearer rect
    def mind(pt,rPts):
        return min(abs(pt[0]-a[0])+abs(pt[1]-a[1]) for a in rPts)
    nr=min(R1,R2,key=lambda e:mind(e,[tuple(a) for a in rects[0][1]]))
    dr,dc = -dc, dc if s else (dc,-dc)   # move away from rect side
    # verify demo behavior: from start, move away; in test, from (3,3) up-right
    if False: pass
    # simpler match demo: from the ENDPOINT NEAREST to rect, step perpendicular INWARD (toward rect), then paint outward opposite side
    # demo: near pt (9,5), inward step would be into rect -> not valid cell; instead paint on OUTSIDE: step away
    # unify: inward candidate = (R1+(sign*dr),R1+(sign*dc)); check if valid bg cell
    incdr=(dr,-dc) if side(R1)!=s else (dr,-dc)
    a,b=nr[0]+incdr[0], nr[1]+incdr[1]
    while 0<=a<H and 0<=b<W and I[a][b]==8:
        out[a][b]=3; a+=incdr[0]; b+=incdr[1]
    return out

I=G['Demo pair 1 input']; O=G['Demo pair 1 output']
print('demo:', f(I)==O)
T=G['Test input']
R=f(T)
new=[(i,j,R[i][j]) for i in range(len(R)) for j in range(len(R[0])) if R[i][j]!=T[i][j]]
for r in R: print(' '.join(map(str,r)))

import os,re,json,collections
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load()

def f(I):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0]); out=[r[:] for r in I]
    g=collections.defaultdict(list)
    for i in range(H):
        for j in range(W): g[I[i][j]].append((i,j))
    bg=max(collections.Counter(p for r in I for p in r).most_common(1)[0][0]) if True else None
    # identify rectangle (largest connected object) and line (other multi-cell)
    bigg=[(col,len(v)) for col,v in g.items() if col!=bg]
    bigg.sort(key=lambda x:-x[1])
    assert len(bigg)>=2
    rc,bigc=bigg[0]; linec,linen=bigg[1]
    pts=set(g[linec])
    ps=sorted(pts,key=lambda p:p[0])
    # line direction
    dr=ps[1][0]-ps[0][0]; dc=ps[1][1]-ps[0][1]
    assert dr==dc
    R=(rc[0][0]+rc[0][1])//2, (rc[0][1])+max(a[1] for a in pts)-min(a[1] for a in pts)   # approximate rect bbox
    def dist(pt):
        return min(abs(pt[0]-a[0])+abs(pt[1]-a[1]) for a in g[rc])
    near=min(ps, key=dist)
    perp=[(-dr,-dc),(dr,dc)]
    best=None
    for dp in perp:
        a,b=near[0]+dp[0],near[1]+dp[1]
        while 0<=a<H and 0<=b<W and I[a][b]==bg:
            best=(a,b,dp); a+=dp[0]; b+=dp[1]
    if best:
        a,b,dp=best
        while 0<=a<H and 0<=b<W and I[a][b]==bg:
            out[a][b]=3; a+=dp[0]; b+=dp[1]
    return out

I=G['Demo pair 1 input']; O=G['Demo pair 1 output']
print('demo match:', f(I)==O)
T=G['Test input']; R=f(T)
new=[(i,j) for i in range(len(R)) for j in range(len(R[0])) if R[i][j]==3]
for r in R: print(' '.join(map(str,r)))

def f(I):
    H=len(I); W=len(I[0]); out=[r[:] for r in I]
    cnt=collections.Counter(p for r in I for p in r)
    bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    g=collections.defaultdict(list)
    for i in range(H):
        for j in range(W): g[I[i][j]].append((i,j))
    bigg=sorted(g.items(), key=lambda kv:-len(kv[1]))
    # bar = largest object, line = next biggest multi-cell object
    barc,bigp=bigg[0]; lcol,lp=bigg[1]
    ps=set(lp)
    ps=sorted(ps,key=lambda p:(p[0]-min(q[0] for q in lp),p[1]-min(q[1] for q in lp)))
    v=(ps[-1][0]-ps[0][0], ps[-1][1]-ps[0][1])
    assert v!=(-v[0],-v[1]) or len(ps)==1
    def ray(a,b,d):
        aa,bb=a+d[0],b+d[1]
        while 0<=aa<H and 0<=bb<W and I[aa][bb]==bg:
            out[aa][bb]=3; aa+=d[0]; bb+=d[1]
    # extend at each endpoint of the line in the line's direction and opposite
    for e,p in [(ps[0],v),(ps[-1],-v)]:
        for d in (v,-v):
            ray(e[0],e[1],d)
    return out
print('demo1:', f(G['Demo pair 1 input'])==G['Demo pair 1 output'])

    if all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
        G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]

def solve(I):
    H=len(I);W=len(I[0]);out=[r[:] for r in I]
    cnt=collections.Counter(v for row in I for v in row)
    bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    # find shape objects: line color vs bar color by counts
    cc=collections.Counter(v for row in I for v in row)
    # assume two object colors besides bg
    objs=sorted({v:c for v,c in cc.items() if v!=bg}.items(), key=lambda kv:-kv[1])
    barc,objp=objs[0]; ocl,onp=objs[1]
    pts=sorted(onp)
    dr=pts[-1][0]-pts[0][0]; dc=pts[-1][1]-pts[0][1]

        steps=[(-1,1),(1,-1)]      # anti-diagonal directions

            while 0<=y<H and 0<=x<W and I[y][x]==bg:
                out[y][x]=3; y+=da; x+=DB
    return out
